title: In-situ Control of the Photon-Magnon Synchronized Mode in a Miniaturized Magnetometer
authors: Yuting Shi, Xudong Wang, Yue Zhao, Lijun Yan, Bimu Yao, Shishen Yan, Lihui Bai, Jinwei Rao
abstract: Photon-magnon synchronized modes (PMSMs) provide a route for magnetic-field sensing by exploiting their enhanced field responsivity due to cusp points (CPs). However, the previous PMSM magnetometer relies on bulky discrete components and lacks in situ control of photon-magnon interactions, limiting its integration and adaptability. Here, we demonstrate a miniaturized PMSM magnetometer integrated on a printed circuit board. A variable resistor is used to tune the photon-magnon coupling strength in situ. By adjusting the variable resistor, the electromagnetic boundary condition of the magnetometer is altered; hence, the reservoir-mediated photon-magnon interaction is changed. The coupling strength shows a non-monotonic dependence on the reflection coefficient adjusted by the variable resistor and reaches its minimum at the impedance matching condition. Furthermore, we develop a non-Hermitian model with standing-wave interference to describe the PMSM dispersion and derive the critical condition for CP formation. This work realizes a compact and tunable PMSM magnetometer and provides a pathway for controlling photon-magnon interactions in integrated magnetic sensing systems.
summary: This paper presents a miniaturized and highly tunable magnetometer based on Photon-Magnon Synchronized Modes (PMSMs). By integrating a variable resistor, the authors achieve in-situ control over the photon-magnon coupling strength by altering the electromagnetic boundary conditions. This work provides a pathway for developing compact, electrically controllable magnetic sensing devices.
main_problem: The goal is to develop a miniaturized and tunable magnetometer based on Photon-Magnon Synchronized Modes (PMSMs) to enhance magnetic-field sensing while overcoming the limitations of bulky, non-tunable existing devices.
main_result: The authors successfully realized a compact and tunable PMSM magnetometer, demonstrating that the photon-magnon coupling strength can be controlled in situ by adjusting the device's electrical impedance.
method: The study combines experimental measurements on a PCB-integrated device with theoretical modeling using a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a miniaturized PMSM magnetometer integrating a YIG sphere (magnon source) and a planar cavity/CPW (photon source). The dynamics are modeled using a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, incorporating reservoir-mediated effects via a variable resistor (VR) that tunes the reflection coefficient ($\Gamma$).
key_observables: The primary observables include the PMSM detuning ($\Delta\omega_s$), the coupling strength ($|g|$), and the magnetic-field-dependent spectral shift ($d(\omega/2\pi)/dI$).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the reflection coefficient ($\Gamma$), the VR resistance ($R$), and the magnetic field/coil current ($I$), which are used to tune the system's coupling and operating point.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian and analyzing the system's steady state using a cubic equation derived under assumptions about fixed phase differences.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device schematic showing the VR for tuning $\Gamma$, the Hamiltonian structure, and experimental results showing how the PMSM detuning and coupling strength vary as a function of the VR setting ($\Gamma$) and the applied magnetic field current ($I$).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical problem and the miniaturized device. It develops the theoretical framework using a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian to describe the coupled photon-magnon interaction. The core of the work demonstrates the tunability by analyzing how the coupling strength and the system's bistability regime can be controlled by adjusting the reflection coefficient $\Gamma$ via the VR.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics because it demonstrates active, electrical control over a fundamental quantum interaction (photon-magnon coupling) in a solid-state, integrated platform, moving beyond passive sensing.

Figure 2 (a) presents a comparison of two emission spectra of our device measured at different magnetic fields. As the coil current is tuned, the magnetic field ex- perienced by the YIG sphere changes. Consequently, the resonant peak in the emission spectrum shifts to a higher frequency, demonstrating the magnetic-field-dependent response of the PMSM. To further characterize the in situ tunability of our device with respect to the mag- netic field and the reflection coefficient, we performed measurements at three different VR resistance values. Spintronics.note: The paper directly models the coupling between magnons (spin waves) and cavity photons using a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, which is central to the field of magnon/photon polaritons and hybrid spin-photon systems.
